Part 6 of Block Diffusion RooflinesPrevious: 5 · The whole pictureNext: 7 · Worked examples

The propositions give closed forms, but only under simplifying assumptions. The calculator below drops the simplifications of (A2): it evaluates every pass of a generation with the exact accounting of the appendix, still under the roofline (A1) and, unless measured routing is chosen, (A5), for any accelerator, model, attention layout and decoding setup. For the chosen setting, it reports both throughputs, the AR batch that matches TD, the memory each decoder needs, and the maps of Part 5. In addition, the page address records the setting, so it can be shared.

Accelerator specs
Model specs

Layer \(\ell\) (counted from 1) is global when \(\ell\) is a multiple of "Global every" (1: all global). "Window" is in tokens and counts the query's own token: it is \(w + 1\) (1,024 for DiffusionGemma).

Sparse attention

\(\zeta\) is the fraction of a canvas's selections that are independent: 1 is the independent case of (A5), and 1/\(b\) means every query selects the same tokens.

Throughput and gain cover the whole generation, during which the context grows from \(P\) to \(P + G\). The regime label and the per-pass table use the context halfway through, \(P + G/2\).

More settings

\(\lambda\) counts the logit-sized reads and writes of HBM per output position (appendix); 0 means the logits stay on-chip.

How many times a pass reads each cached byte from memory: 1 when the attention kernel reads the cache once.

How the numbers are counted

    
Every gain in Parts 1–7 is a ratio of roofline bounds, counted in one of three ways.

    
A roofline time is a lower bound on the time of a pass, so each throughput is an upper bound, and \(\Gamma\) is the ratio of two such bounds, not a measurement. Part 11 compares these bounds with throughput measured in vLLM. The three accountings below differ in what they include, and each number in the blogpost says which one it uses. For DiffusionGemma on an H200:

    

    
In the interactive figures and the cards, the intensities \(\class{mj-ar}{I_{AR}}\) and \(\class{mj-td}{I_{TD}}\) are those of Definition 3, without the vocabulary, except in the intensity tabs of Figure 20 and the calculator's maps, which use the exact accounting of the appendix; next to an exact gain, the regime of a pass is given instead as the share of the peak compute that it uses. The cards quote the closed-form values of the propositions, at zero context where Part 3 does, unless a readout says exact. A fourth variant, the kernel-by-kernel timing rule of Part 5, can be switched on in Figure 10 and in the calculator.
